newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae, holders agree to joint meeting.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae, holders agree to joint meeting.

text.p: The Student Loan Marketing Association, commonly known as Sallie Mae, and a shareholder group said Tuesday they had agreed to hold a special joint meeting at which shareholders will vote on a plan to privatise and reorganize the association.
The group, the Committee to Restore Value, is opposed to the management of Sallie Mae.
At the meeting, shareholders will also vote to elect a 15-member holding company board from separate slates nominated by Sallie Mae and the committee.

According to a news release, Sallie Mae and the committee will jointly file an amended registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission and will hold the special meeting about 20 days after completion of an SEC review and a mailing of revised materials to shareholders.
According to the release, Sallie Mae and the committee believe the joint meeting approach will ensure approval of privatisation.
At separate meetings earlier this month, both the Sallie Mae management and the committee failed to get a majority of shareholders to back their competing plans.

"We are very pleased and not surprised because it makes sense for the shareholders," said Paul Carey, a committee spokesman. "They (the shareholders) get to approve privatisation and then the shareholders get to select the people who will guide the company in the future and that's the way it should be."
Carey estimated the privatisation would be approved in about 40 days. He said the committee has received about 24 million votes for its plan.
There are 52.8 million Sallie Mae shares outstanding.
The news release said the earlier meetings will not be reconvened and the polls for those meetings are closed.
The release also said Sallie Mae will reimburse the committee for all reasonable proxy-related expenses and drop outstanding litigation. The amount of the reimbursement was not disclosed.
